Redline round 3

Reviewed the fix diff from round 2 (4c8ed6a..e068d94), and the coverage pass's candidates over the whole pull request at e068d94.

The coverage pass over the whole pull request at e068d94 returned 4 candidates: 4 verified, 0 could not be confirmed, 0 refuted, 0 collapsed into items already reported or settled, 0 already tracked.

Round 2's fixes work. The hunk stream is read as text everywhere, the clone's diff reads every wanted file as text, the scratch folder exists before the listing is read, and the harness's own git ignores global and system config; each fix has a case. The findings left are more inputs the new paths assume away: pathspec variables that make the clone's git die, git config passed through the environment that still reaches the fixture's whole diff, a non-object comment that fails before the documented check runs, and a docs sentence this pull request's tests made stale. Nothing in this repository is scheduled or queued against these files, so no overlap applies.

### Correctness (2)

- **R3-1** · correctness · low · confirmed · `scripts/redline-gh.sh:376` · GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS or GIT_GLOB_PATHSPECS in the environment makes the clone's git diff die, so every comment the clone would place goes to the body
- **R3-2** · correctness · low · confirmed · `scripts/redline-gh.sh:723` · A review file whose comments hold a non-object exits 5 with jq's raw error, not the documented exit 2 and line

### Other items (2)

- **R3-3** · nit · low · confirmed · `tests/gh-test.sh:84` · hgit still lets git configuration given through the environment reach the fixture's whole diff
- **R3-4** · nit · low · confirmed · `docs/scripts.md:9` · docs/scripts.md still says the gh harness pins only the read subcommands, resolve-threads and defer

Each item has an inline comment with the detail or, where GitHub could not anchor it, sits under Not placed inline below. Redline replies in the item's thread, or in a PR comment that opens with its marker, with what it decided and why.

comments.body:
**R3-1** · correctness · low · confirmed

**GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS or GIT_GLOB_PATHSPECS in the environment makes the clone's git diff die, so every comment the clone would place goes to the body**

recover_hunks runs the clone's diff as `env -u GIT_DIFF_OPTS git --literal-pathspecs ... diff ...` (lines 376-378), with stderr sent to /dev/null and a failing call skipped. git refuses `--literal-pathspecs` (which sets GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1) beside any other global pathspec setting: its get_global_magic dies with "global 'literal' pathspec setting is incompatible with all other global pathspec settings" when GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS or GIT_GLOB_PATHSPECS is set. That message is in the installed git (/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/bin/git, found with grep -a). So with either variable exported, every per-file diff in the loop at 375-381 fails silently, no section reaches the hunk stream, and place_comments gives each such file the kind "nopatch" (line 443), so its comments move under "The file's patch could not be had from GitHub's listing, its whole diff or this clone:" (line 450) instead of getting a thread. On the harness's PR 21 (301 files, so the clone is the only source) that moves all five comments of review-21.json, where the expected result places R1-1, R1-2 and R1-4. It also applies on a PR of 300 files or fewer whenever the whole diff is refused or lacks a file's section (a path the diff header quotes). I could not run it here: the guard refuses a GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS= prefix for every role; the trace is the code above and git's own message. Conditions: the user's shell exports one of those two variables, which is rare. The header comment at 339-340 says the user's git configuration and environment cannot move a hunk; this is a different variable from R1-4's GIT_DIFF_OPTS (fixed, and that fix holds) and from R2-2's attributes, through another mechanism (git exits instead of moving a hunk), so it is a new finding.

Proposed fix: Unset the pathspec variables on that call alongside GIT_DIFF_OPTS: `env -u GIT_DIFF_OPTS -u GIT_GLOB_PATHSPECS -u GIT_NOGLOB_PATHSPECS -u GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS git --literal-pathspecs ...`, update the header comment and the bash-conventions line that lists what the call runs with, and add a case next to the GIT_DIFF_OPTS=-u0 one in tests/gh-test.sh: `icase="$(GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS=1 gh place 21 "$WORK/review-21.json")"` expecting `[[1500,98,1300],["R1-3","R1-5"]]`, and the same for GIT_GLOB_PATHSPECS=1.

**R3-2** · correctness · low · confirmed

**A review file whose comments hold a non-object exits 5 with jq's raw error, not the documented exit 2 and line**

The post-review header (lines 135-137, quoted verbatim in docs/scripts.md) says comments the placement cannot read stop it before anything is posted with one line on stderr naming the review file and exit 2. The check that keeps that promise (lines 734-737, from R1-9's fix) runs only after recover_hunks (line 723). The up-front check at 707 only tests that `comments` is an array, so `{body: "Redline round 1", comments: [1]}` passes it, and recover_hunks calls wanted_files (line 351), whose jq binds `([$review[0].comments[].path] | unique) as $named` (line 298) before it looks at any file. That binding fails on a number (`jq: error ... Cannot index number with string ("path")`; checked with jq here, and it fails even when the listing is empty), and since recover_hunks runs as a plain command under `set -euo pipefail` (line 183), the script stops with jq's exit 5 and jq's message. Nothing is posted, so R1-9's defect (an empty body posted) does not come back; what is wrong is the exit code and the message the header promises. `place` takes the same path (line 545) and exits 5 too; its header makes no such promise. Conditions: a review file whose comments array holds a non-object, which the workflow's own GitHub agent does not write.

Proposed fix: Extend the up-front check at 707 to `(.body | type == "string") and (.comments | type == "array") and (.comments | all(type == "object"))`, or run `recover_hunks ... || { echo "redline-gh.sh: could not place the comments of $2; nothing was posted" >&2; exit 2; }`; add a gh-test case posting `{body:"Redline round 1",comments:[1]}` to PR 20 that expects exit 2, the one line and no post in the log.

**R3-3** · nit · low · confirmed

**hgit still lets git configuration given through the environment reach the fixture's whole diff**

R2-4 was fixed, but still reproduces through another input. hgit (line 84) sets GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 and unsets GIT_DIFF_OPTS, but git also reads configuration from GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/GIT_CONFIG_KEY_<n>/GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_<n> and from GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS (which git exports to anything it runs under `git -c ...`, an alias or a hook), and neither of those is a global or system file. whole_diff (line 191) pins no -U, algorithm or inter-hunk context, so `diff.context=0` given that way shrinks the hunks of src/big.js in $PAGES/diff-20.txt: line 98 of review-20-text.json is a context line of the hunk around changed line 100 only at -U3, so it moves to the body and the three cases at lines 475-477 ('an added, a removed and a context line stay inline', 'nothing is moved', 'the body is left alone') fail. The R2-4 guard case (line 565) does not catch it: it builds both sides of its cmp under the same environment. The hgit comment (lines 80-83) and the new line in agent-os/standards/testing/tests.md (line 37) say the developer's configuration and environment are shut out. I traced this through the fixture and the cases; I could not run it under GIT_CONFIG_COUNT because the guard refuses an environment prefix. Conditions: a developer whose environment carries git configuration that way, a local-only failure; CI is unaffected.

Proposed fix: In hgit also `env -u GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS -u GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, and/or pin `-U3 --inter-hunk-context=0 --diff-algorithm=myers` in whole_diff; make the R2-4 case compare against a diff made under a clean environment with GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=diff.context GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=0 on the rebuilt side.

**R3-4** · nit · low · confirmed

**docs/scripts.md still says the gh harness pins only the read subcommands, resolve-threads and defer**

docs/scripts.md line 9 says `tests/gh-test.sh` pins 'the read subcommands, `resolve-threads` and `defer`'. On the base that was true (the shim refused every write but two). This pull request makes the shim answer PR 20's review POST and adds the `# post-review: a refusal the new sources can cause (#96)` section with the too-large, fallback, no-status, unplaceable and temp-file cases, and the harness's own header and agent-os/standards/testing/tests.md now say so. So a reader looking for where post-review's retry behaviour is tested is told it is not. The sentence is outside this pull request's hunks of docs/scripts.md (which start at line 12); the cause is this pull request's new tests.

Proposed fix: Update the `redline-gh.sh` section of `docs/scripts.md` (line 9): name `post-review` among what `tests/gh-test.sh` pins.

The cause is in code this pull request did not change.
